subject: maths
title: Primary 5 Percentage: Parts of a Whole and Percentage of a Quantity
seo_title: P5 Percentage Worksheets: Free Primary 5 Maths Practice with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Expressing a part of a whole as a percentage; use of %; finding a percentage part of a whole
meta_desc: Free P5 percentage practice: hundred squares, fractions and decimals as %, 18 out of 40 as a percentage, 25% of $60. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Percentage means out of 100: part ÷ whole × 100%.
body_html:
Percentage means “out of 100”

A percentage is a part of a whole, written out of 100. The sign % means per cent. 100% is the whole. 37% means 37 out of 100.

Fractions and decimals as percentages

Make the denominator 100, or multiply by 100%.

Example

Write 35 as a percentage.

Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 20: 35 = 60100.

Answer: 60%

Example

Write 0.08 as a percentage.

0.08 × 100% = 8%. (0.08 is 8 hundredths.)

Answer: 8%

A part of a whole as a percentage

Put the part over the whole, then multiply by 100%.

Example

Express 18 out of 40 as a percentage.

1840 × 100% = 45%. Or: 1840 = 920 = 45100.

Answer: 45%

Use the same unit for the part and the whole: 50 cm out of 2 m = 50 cm out of 200 cm = 25%.

A percentage of a quantity

Write the percentage as a fraction out of 100 and multiply. A bar model helps.

Example

Find 25% of $60.

25100 × $60 = $15.

Answer: $15

Example

A class has 40 students. 45% are boys. How many girls are there?

Girls: 100% − 45% = 55%. 55100 × 40 = 22.

Answer: 22 girls

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
35 = 35%Make the denominator 100: 35 = 60100 = 60%
18 out of 40: 40 ÷ 18Part over whole: 1840 × 100% = 45%
25% of 60 = 60 − 25 = 3525100 × 60 = 15
18 out of 40 = 18%18% means 18 out of 100. The whole here is 40
0.08 = 80%0.08 is 8 hundredths: 0.08 × 100% = 8%

faq.q: What is taught in P5 percentage?
faq.a: Primary 5 students learn that percentage means out of 100, change fractions and decimals to percentages, express a part of a whole as a percentage and find a percentage of a quantity, such as 25% of $60.

faq.q: How do I explain percentage to my child?
faq.a: Start with a hundred square: 37 squares shaded out of 100 is 37%. Then use a bar model: split $60 into 4 equal units, so 25% is 1 unit, $15.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with percentage?
faq.a: Writing the numbers of a fraction side by side, such as 3/5 = 35%. Make the denominator 100 instead: 3/5 = 60/100 = 60%.

faq.q: Is percentage in the MOE syllabus for Primary 5?
faq.a: Yes. Percentage is a Primary 5 topic in the MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics Syllabus, and it is built on in Primary 6 for the PSLE.

sets.title: Percentage means out of 100: hundred squares

items.q: The hundred square has 100 equal squares. What percentage of it is shaded?
items.e: 37 out of 100 squares are shaded: 37100 = 37%. 63% is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: The hundred square has 100 equal squares. What percentage of it is shaded?
items.e: 8 out of 100 squares are shaded: 8100 = 8%. 8 squares are shaded, not 8 columns. 92% is not shaded.

items.q: The hundred square has 100 equal squares. What percentage of it is shaded?
items.e: 45 out of 100 squares are shaded: 45100 = 45%. Count the full columns first: 4 columns = 40 squares, then 5 more.

items.q: The hundred square has 100 equal squares. What percentage of it is not shaded?
items.e: 28 out of 100 squares are not shaded: 28100 = 28%. 72% is the shaded part. 100 − 72 = 28, not 38: rename 1 ten as 10 ones.

items.q: The hundred square has 100 equal squares. What percentage of it is shaded?
items.e: 16 out of 100 squares are shaded: 16100 = 16%. 1 full column (10 squares) and 6 more. 84% is not shaded.

items.q: The hundred square has 100 equal squares. What percentage of it is not shaded?
items.e: 10 out of 100 squares are not shaded: 10100 = 10%. 90 squares are shaded, so 10 squares are not shaded. 9 is the number of shaded columns.

items.q: The hundred square has 100 equal squares. What percentage of it is shaded?
items.e: 100 out of 100 squares are shaded: 100100 = 100%. All 100 squares are shaded. That is the whole: 100%.

items.q: What is 29 out of 100 as a percentage?
items.e: Per cent means out of 100, so 29 out of 100 = 29100 = 29%. 71% is the rest of the 100.

items.q: Write 9% as a fraction.
items.e: 9% means 9 out of 100: 9100. 910 would be 90%.

items.q: Write 3100 as a percentage.
items.e: 3100 means 3 out of 100, so it is 3%. 30% would be 310.

items.q: Which is the same as 40%?
items.e: Per cent means out of 100, so 40% = 40 out of 100. 60 out of 100 is the other part.

items.q: What does per cent mean?
items.e: “Per cent” means out of 100. 7% is 7 out of 100. The sign % stands for “per cent”.

items.q: 64 out of every 100 students in a school wear spectacles. What percentage of the students do not wear spectacles?
items.e: The whole is 100%. 100% − 64% = 36%. 46% is a renaming mistake: 100 − 64 = 36.

items.q: Find the missing percentage: 45% + ? = 100%
items.e: 100% − 45% = 55%. Check: 45 + 55 = 100. 65% is a renaming mistake.

items.q: In a hundred square, 30 squares are red and 25 squares are blue. The rest are white. What percentage of the squares are white?
items.e: Red and blue: 30 + 25 = 55 squares = 55%. White: 100% − 55% = 45%. 55% is red and blue together.

items.q: A hawker centre has 100 tables. 83 tables are taken. What percentage of the tables are empty?
items.e: 100 − 83 = 17 empty tables out of 100, so 17%. 83% of the tables are taken.

items.q: Which is the largest part of a whole?
items.e: All of them are out of 100. 90 out of 100 is the most, so 90% is the largest.

items.q: Ali shaded 7 squares of a hundred square. Mei Ling shaded 30% of another hundred square. How many more squares did Mei Ling shade than Ali?
items.e: 30% of a hundred square is 30 squares. 30 − 7 = 23. 37 adds instead of subtracts.

items.q: A packet has 100 beads. 4 of the beads are broken. What percentage of the beads are broken?
items.e: 4 out of 100 = 4100 = 4%. 96% of the beads are not broken. 40% would be 40 beads.

items.q: How many squares must you shade to show 1% of a hundred square?
items.e: 1% means 1 out of 100, so shade 1 square. 10 squares would be 10%.

items.q: Write 310 as a percentage.
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 10 to make the denominator 100: 310 = 30100 = 30%. Or: 310 × 100% = 30%. Do not write the numerator as the percentage.

items.q: Write 14 as a percentage.
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 25 to make the denominator 100: 14 = 25100 = 25%. Or: 14 × 100% = 25%. Do not join the 1 and the 4 together. 75% is the other three quarters.

items.q: Write 35 as a percentage.
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 20 to make the denominator 100: 35 = 60100 = 60%. Or: 35 × 100% = 60%. 35 is not 35%: do not write the 3 and the 5 together.

items.q: Write 720 as a percentage.
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 5 to make the denominator 100: 720 = 35100 = 35%. Or: 720 × 100% = 35%. Do not add 7 and 20. 65% is the other part.

items.q: Write 34 as a percentage.
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 25 to make the denominator 100: 34 = 75100 = 75%. Or: 34 × 100% = 75%. Do not join the 3 and the 4. 25% is the part that is left.

items.q: Write 925 as a percentage.
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 4 to make the denominator 100: 925 = 36100 = 36%. Or: 925 × 100% = 36%. 9% would be 9 out of 100. 34 is 9 + 25.

items.q: Write 45 as a percentage.
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 20 to make the denominator 100: 45 = 80100 = 80%. Or: 45 × 100% = 80%. 45 is not 45%. 20% is the other fifth.

items.q: Write 15 as a percentage.
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 20 to make the denominator 100: 15 = 20100 = 20%. Or: 15 × 100% = 20%. Do not join the 1 and the 5. 5% would be 1 out of 20.

items.q: Write 1350 as a percentage.
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 2 to make the denominator 100: 1350 = 26100 = 26%. Or: 1350 × 100% = 26%. 13% would be 13 out of 100. 63 is 13 + 50.

items.q: Write 1120 as a percentage.
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 5 to make the denominator 100: 1120 = 55100 = 55%. Or: 1120 × 100% = 55%. 11% would be 11 out of 100. 45% is the other part.

items.q: Write 225 as a percentage.
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 4 to make the denominator 100: 225 = 8100 = 8%. Or: 225 × 100% = 8%. 2% would be 2 out of 100. 92% is the other part.

items.q: Write 1920 as a percentage.
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 5 to make the denominator 100: 1920 = 95100 = 95%. Or: 1920 × 100% = 95%. 19% would be 19 out of 100. 5% is the part that is left.

items.q: Write 0.4 as a percentage.
items.e: 0.4 × 100% = 40%. 0.4 = 4 tenths = 40 hundredths. 4% would be 0.04.

items.q: Write 0.75 as a percentage.
items.e: 0.75 × 100% = 75%. Multiply by 100, not by 10. 25% is the part that is left.

items.q: Write 0.08 as a percentage.
items.e: 0.08 × 100% = 8%. 0.08 is 8 hundredths, not 8 tenths. 80% would be 0.8.

items.q: Write 0.36 as a percentage.
items.e: 0.36 × 100% = 36%. Move the digits two places to the left (× 100), not one.

items.q: Write 0.5 as a percentage.
items.e: 0.5 × 100% = 50%. 0.5 = 5 tenths = 50 hundredths. 5% would be 0.05.

items.q: Write 35% as a fraction in its simplest form.
items.e: 35% = 35100. Divide the numerator and the denominator by 5: 720. 710 = 70%.

items.q: Write 6% as a decimal.
items.e: 6% = 6100 = 6 hundredths = 0.06. 0.6 is 6 tenths = 60%.

items.q: Which is the greatest?
items.e: Write them all as percentages: 1320 = 65%, 0.6 = 60%, 0.58 = 58%. The greatest is 1320.

sets.title: Express a part of a whole as a percentage

items.q: What percentage of the grid is shaded?
items.e: 7 of the 20 squares are shaded. 720 = 35100 = 35%. There are 20 squares, not 100, so it is not 7%.

items.q: The bar has 8 equal parts. What percentage of the bar is shaded?
items.e: 2 of the 8 parts are shaded. 28 = 14 = 25100 = 25%. 4% comes from 8 ÷ 2: do not divide the whole by the part.

items.q: What percentage of the grid is not shaded?
items.e: 25 squares, 9 shaded, so 16 are not shaded. 1625 = 64100 = 64%. 36% is the shaded part.

items.q: Express 18 out of 40 as a percentage.
items.e: 1840 = 920 = 45100 = 45%. 18% would be 18 out of 100. 55% is the other part.

items.q: Express 5 out of 20 as a percentage.
items.e: 520 = 25100 = 25%. 4% comes from 20 ÷ 5: do not divide the whole by the part.

items.q: Express 12 out of 60 as a percentage.
items.e: 1260 = 15 = 20100 = 20%. 5% comes from 60 ÷ 12: put the part on top, the whole at the bottom.

items.q: Express 9 out of 30 as a percentage.
items.e: 930 = 310 = 30100 = 30%. 9% would be 9 out of 100. 21 is 30 − 9, not a percentage.

items.q: Express 21 out of 35 as a percentage.
items.e: 2135 = 35 = 60100 = 60%. 21% would be 21 out of 100. 40% is the other part.

items.q: Express 27 out of 36 as a percentage.
items.e: 2736 = 34 = 75100 = 75%. 27% would be 27 out of 100. 25% is the other part.

items.q: Express 33 out of 300 as a percentage.
items.e: 33300 = 11100 = 11%. The whole is 300, not 100. 89% is the other part.

items.q: Express 72 out of 400 as a percentage.
items.e: 72400 = 950 = 18100 = 18%. 36% comes from dividing by 2 only: 36200 is not out of 100. 72% would be 72 out of 100.

items.q: Express 120 out of 500 as a percentage.
items.e: 120500 = 625 = 24100 = 24%. 12% drops a zero. 120% would be 120 out of 100. 76% is the other part.

items.q: Express 15 out of 75 as a percentage.
items.e: 1575 = 15 = 20100 = 20%. 5% comes from 75 ÷ 15: do not divide the whole by the part.

items.q: What percentage of $50 is $12?
items.e: 1250 = 24100 = 24%. Do not write $12 as 12%: the whole is $50, not $100.

items.q: What percentage of 2 m is 50 cm?
items.e: Use the same unit: 2 m = 200 cm. 50200 = 14 = 25100 = 25%. 50% forgets to change 2 m to 200 cm.

items.q: What percentage of 1 kg is 300 g?
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. 3001000 = 310 = 30100 = 30%. 300% forgets to change 1 kg to 1000 g.

items.q: What percentage of 1 h is 15 min?
items.e: 1 h = 60 min. 1560 = 14 = 25100 = 25%. 1 h has 60 min, not 100 min, so it is not 15%.

items.q: What percentage of 2 ℓ is 400 ml?
items.e: 2 ℓ = 2000 ml. 4002000 = 15 = 20100 = 20%. 40% uses 1000 ml instead of 2000 ml.

items.q: Which is the greater percentage: 6 out of 8 or 14 out of 20?
items.e: 68 = 75%. 1420 = 70%. 75% > 70%, so 6 out of 8 is greater, even though 14 is more than 6.

items.q: Which calculation expresses 18 out of 40 as a percentage?
items.e: Put the part (18) over the whole (40), then multiply by 100%: 1840 × 100% = 45%. 4018 divides the whole by the part.

sets.title: Find a percentage of a quantity

items.q: The bar model shows $60 in 4 equal units. What is 25% of $60?
items.e: 4 units = 100% = $60, so 1 unit = 25% = $60 ÷ 4 = $15. 25% of $60 = 25100 × $60 = $15. $35 is $60 − 25: 25% is not 25 dollars. $45 is the other 75%.

items.q: Find 10% of 80.
items.e: 10% of 80 = 10100 × 80 = 8. 10% means ÷ 10, not ÷ 100. Do not take away 10.

items.q: Find 50% of 64.
items.e: 50% of 64 = 50100 × 64 = 32. 50% is a half, not double. 14 is 64 − 50.

items.q: Find 20% of 150.
items.e: 20% of 150 = 20100 × 150 = 30. 130 is 150 − 20. 7.5 is 150 ÷ 20. 120 is the other 80%.

items.q: Find 75% of 48.
items.e: 75% of 48 = 75100 × 48 = 36. 12 is only 25% and 24 is 50%. 64 is 48 ÷ 34.

items.q: Find 30% of 90.
items.e: 30% of 90 = 30100 × 90 = 27. 60 is 90 − 30. 3 is 90 ÷ 30. 9 is only 10%.

items.q: Find 15% of 200.
items.e: 15% of 200 = 15100 × 200 = 30. 185 is 200 − 15. 20 is only 10%. 15 forgets that the whole is 200, not 100.

items.q: Find 5% of 360.
items.e: 5% of 360 = 5100 × 360 = 18. 72 is 360 ÷ 5, which is 20%. 36 is 10%.

items.q: Find 12% of 50.
items.e: 12% of 50 = 12100 × 50 = 6. 38 is 50 − 12. 5 is only 10%. 44 is the other 88%.

items.q: Find 35% of 400 ml.
items.e: 35% of 400 ml = 35100 × 400 ml = 140 ml. 365 ml is 400 − 35. 260 ml is the other 65%.

items.q: Find 90% of 70.
items.e: 90% of 70 = 90100 × 70 = 63. 7 is the 10% that is left out. 60 is 70 − 10.

items.q: Find 1% of 900.
items.e: 1% of 900 = 1100 × 900 = 9. 1% means ÷ 100. 90 would be 10%.

items.q: Find 45% of 80.
items.e: 45% of 80 = 45100 × 80 = 36. 44 is the other 55%. 35 is 80 − 45. 32 is only 40%.

items.q: Find 40% of $35.
items.e: 40% of $35 = 40100 × $35 = $14. $21 is the other 60%. $3.50 is only 10%.

items.q: Find 8% of $250.
items.e: 8% of $250 = 8100 × $250 = $20. $200 is 80%. $242 is $250 − 8. $25 is only 10%.

items.q: Find 60% of 2 kg. Give your answer in grams.
items.e: 2 kg = 2000 g. 60% of 2000 g = 60100 × 2000 g = 1200 g. 800 g is the other 40%.

items.q: Find 25% of 1 ℓ. Give your answer in millilitres.
items.e: 1 ℓ = 1000 ml. 25% of 1000 ml = 25100 × 1000 ml = 250 ml. 40 ml is 1000 ÷ 25. 750 ml is the other 75%.

items.q: Find 70% of 3 m. Give your answer in centimetres.
items.e: 3 m = 300 cm. 70% of 300 cm = 70100 × 300 cm = 210 cm. 90 cm is the other 30%. 230 cm is 300 − 70.

items.q: The bar model shows 240 in 10 equal units. What is 30% of 240?
Which calculation finds 25% of 60?
items.e: 25% = 25100, so 25% of 60 = 25100 × 60 = 15. 60 ÷ 25 divides by the percentage instead.

sets.title: Percentage word problems: test marks, surveys and savings

items.q: Mei Ling scored 36 out of 40 marks in a maths test. What percentage of the marks did she score?
items.e: 3640 = 910 = 90100 = 90%. 9% comes from 3640 = 910: that is 9 tenths, not 9 hundredths. 10% is the part she did not score.

items.q: In a class survey, 14 of the 40 students chose chicken rice as their favourite hawker food. What percentage of the students chose chicken rice?
items.e: 1440 = 720 = 35100 = 35%. 14% would be 14 out of 100. 65% chose other food.

items.q: 200 students were asked how they travel to school. 35% of them take the MRT. How many students take the MRT?
items.e: 35% of 200 = 35100 × 200 = 70. 35 would be 35 out of 100, but there are 200 students. 130 is the other 65%.

items.q: Hafiz gets $60 of pocket money a month. He saves 20% of it. How much does he save each month?
Siti had $150. She saved $45 of it. What percentage of her money did she save?
items.e: 45150 = 310 = 30100 = 30%. 0.3% forgets to multiply 45150 = 0.3 by 100%. 70% is the part she did not save.

items.q: There are 40 students in a class. 45% of them are boys. How many girls are there?
items.e: Girls: 100% − 45% = 55%. 55% of 40 = 55100 × 40 = 22. 18 is the number of boys. 55 is the percentage of girls, not the number.

items.q: Mrs Ng bought 80 mandarin oranges for Chinese New Year. She gave 20% of them to her neighbours. How many oranges did she have left?
items.e: 5 units = 100% = 80, so 1 unit = 20% = 80 ÷ 5 = 16. She gave away 1 unit and kept 4 units: 4 × 16 = 64. 16 is the number she gave away. 60 is 80 − 20. 20 is 80 ÷ 4.

items.q: In a class of 40 students, 30% take the school bus and 45% come by car. The rest walk to school. How many students walk?
items.e: Walk: 100% − 30% − 45% = 25%. 25% of 40 = 40 ÷ 4 = 10. 25 is the percentage, not the number of students. 12 take the bus and 18 come by car.

items.q: 250 students ran in a race on Sports Day. 92% of them finished the race. How many students did not finish?
items.e: Did not finish: 100% − 92% = 8%. 8% of 250 = 8100 × 250 = 20. 230 finished. 8 is the percentage, not the number.

items.q: Ryan answered 25 questions in a quiz. He got 20 of them correct. What percentage of the questions did he get wrong?
items.e: He got 25 − 20 = 5 wrong. 525 = 20100 = 20%. 80% is the percentage he got correct.

items.q: A water tank holds 500 ℓ when it is full. It is 60% full. How much water is in the tank?
items.e: 5 units = 100% = 500 ℓ, so 1 unit = 20% = 100 ℓ. 60% is 3 units = 300 ℓ. 200 ℓ is the empty part. 440 ℓ is 500 − 60. 30 ℓ is only 6%.

items.q: A school has 800 students. 15% of them are in a uniformed group CCA. How many students is that?
items.e: 15% of 800 = 15100 × 800 = 120. 785 is 800 − 15. 680 is the other 85%.

items.q: A class library has 250 books. 40 of them are borrowed. What percentage of the books are borrowed?
items.e: 40250 = 425 = 16100 = 16%. 40% would be 40 out of 100. 0.16% forgets to multiply by 100%.

items.q: Priya had 1 ℓ of orange juice. She drank 30% of it. How much juice was left? Give your answer in millilitres.
items.e: 1 ℓ = 1000 ml. 30% of 1000 ml = 300 ml. Left: 1000 ml − 300 ml = 700 ml. 300 ml is what she drank. 970 ml is 1000 − 30.

items.q: Jun Jie had $20 on his EZ-Link card. He used 35% of it on bus and MRT rides. How much was left on the card?
items.e: 35% of $20 = 35100 × $20 = $7. Left: $20 − $7 = $13. $7 is the amount used. $14 takes away only 30%. $65 is 100 − 35: the money is $20, not $100.

items.q: A fruit stall had 120 durians. 75% of them were sold. How many durians were left?
items.e: 4 units = 120, so 1 unit = 120 ÷ 4 = 30. 3 units were sold and 1 unit is left: 30. 90 were sold. 45 is 120 − 75. 25 is the percentage left, not the number.

items.q: Wei Ming scored 42 out of 50 in English and 17 out of 20 in science. In which test did he score the higher percentage?
items.e: English: 4250 = 84100 = 84%. Science: 1720 = 85100 = 85%. 85% > 84%, so science, even though he scored more marks in English.

items.q: Zhi Hao had $50. He spent 40% of it on a book and 10% of it on bubble tea. How much money did he have left?
items.e: He spent 40% + 10% = 50%. He had 50% left: 50% of $50 = $25. $20 is the cost of the book and $5 is the bubble tea. $30 only takes away the book.

items.q: Xin Yi received $200 in red packets at Chinese New Year. She saved 65% of the money in the bank. How much money did she save?
items.e: 65% of $200 = 65100 × $200 = $130. $70 is what she did not save. $135 is $200 − 65.

items.q: 25 students voted for a class outing. 8 chose Sentosa, 12 chose Gardens by the Bay and the rest chose the Singapore Zoo. What percentage of the students chose the Singapore Zoo?
items.e: Zoo: 25 − 8 − 12 = 5 students. 525 = 20100 = 20%. 5% would be 5 out of 100. 48% chose Gardens by the Bay.
